issues.t: Cam phaser and timing chain rattle
issues.sym: A ticking, knocking or diesel-like rattle from the engine, mostly at idle or just above it, sometimes with rough running, a check engine light and loss of power.
issues.why: The 3-valve 5.4L uses oil-pressure-driven cam phasers and long timing chains. Worn phasers, low oil pressure or worn chain tensioners and guides let parts rattle. Ford issued a bulletin for an intermittent engine rattle from idle to 1,200 rpm on these trucks.
issues.next: Use the correct oil and change it on time, since this engine is sensitive to oil condition. Have the noise diagnosed early; replacing phasers, chains and tensioners before something breaks can prevent a ruined engine.

issues.t: Spark plugs break off during removal
issues.sym: During a routine tune-up, one or more spark plugs snap off in the cylinder head, turning a simple job into a major repair.
issues.why: This engine uses a long two-piece spark plug whose lower shell can seize in the head with carbon. When removed, the plug can break and leave part of it stuck in the cylinder.
issues.next: Have plugs changed by a shop that knows this engine and uses the factory procedure and an extraction tool. Do not stretch the change interval too long, and ask for a quote that covers broken-plug removal.

issues.t: Misfire from a failed ignition coil or plug boot
issues.sym: Check engine light (sometimes flashing), shaking at idle and rough running; codes often point to a single cylinder.
issues.why: Each cylinder has its own coil-on-plug. A worn coil or boot can arc and cause a misfire. Ford also noted mismatched boots on some remanufactured engines of this type.
issues.next: A flashing check engine light means stop driving hard, as it can damage the catalytic converter. Have the misfiring cylinder found and the coil, boot and plug replaced as needed.

issues.t: Engine loses power or runs poorly
issues.sym: The truck suddenly lacks power, hesitates or idles roughly, sometimes with a wrench or check engine light, usually at higher mileage.
issues.why: Owners report power loss at around 120,000 miles. On this engine common causes include a failing electronic throttle body, cam phaser problems or misfires; Ford also issued guidance to help dealers diagnose throttle body concerns.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the throttle body, phasers and ignition checked. Fix it promptly, since some causes get worse over time.

issues.t: Front hubs grind or stay engaged in 2WD
issues.sym: On 4x4 trucks, a grinding or ratcheting noise from the front wheels in 2WD that stops when you shift into 4x4.
issues.why: The vacuum-operated front hubs (integrated wheel ends) may not fully disengage in 2WD, often because of a vacuum leak, failed solenoid or worn hub parts. Ford issued bulletins for this on these trucks.
issues.next: Driving in 4x4 briefly may quiet it, but have the vacuum lines, solenoid and hub seals checked so the hubs do not wear out.

issues.t: Hard starts and unstable idle after the battery is disconnected
issues.sym: After a battery replacement or a dead battery, the engine is hard to start, the idle speed hunts up and down, and idle-related codes may set.
issues.why: The engine computer loses its learned idle settings when power is cut and has trouble relearning them. Ford issued a bulletin for this condition.
issues.next: Let the engine idle with accessories off so it can relearn. If it continues, a shop can clean the throttle body and run the relearn procedure.

issues.t: Erratic fuel gauge with check engine light
issues.sym: The fuel gauge jumps around or reads wrong, and the check engine light may come on with fuel-level codes.
issues.why: A fault in the fuel level sensing circuit in the tank or the instrument cluster. Ford issued bulletins for trucks built before December 2007.
issues.next: Track your mileage between fill-ups so you do not run dry. Have a dealer check the bulletins, as the fix may be a sender or cluster repair.

issues.t: Power steering pressure line seeps fluid in cold weather
issues.sym: Power steering fluid wet spots on the high-pressure line or drips under the front, often in cold climates; you may hear a whine if the level gets low.
issues.why: Ford found the high-pressure power steering line could seep at its fittings in cold weather.
issues.next: Keep the power steering fluid topped up and have the line inspected. Replacing the line stops the seep.

issues.sym: Water dripping inside near the moonroof, wind noise, or noise when opening and closing it.
issues.why: The moonroof glass can sit at the wrong height or position, and drains can clog. Ford issued adjustment procedures for this.
issues.next: Clear the drain tubes and have the glass height and position adjusted. Dry any wet carpet quickly to prevent mold and electrical problems.

issues.t: Automatic transmission whine, slipping or no reverse
issues.sym: Grinding, whining or vibration from the transmission, slipping in third, no fourth gear, the overdrive-off light flashing, or loss of reverse.
issues.why: On the 4-speed automatic, the planetary gear set and direct clutch can fail. Ford released bulletins and a service kit for these failures.
issues.next: Stop towing and have it diagnosed soon. Planetary gear damage usually means a transmission rebuild.

issues.t: Vibration from a parking brake that does not fully release
issues.sym: An intermittent vibration while driving that may be linked to the parking brake.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for vibration caused by the parking brake not fully disengaging.
issues.next: Make sure the parking brake releases fully. If the vibration continues, have the rear parking brake shoes and cables checked.

issues.t: Brake booster vacuum hose can blow off (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal suddenly becomes very hard and the truck takes longer to stop.
issues.why: On trucks with the 5.4L 3-valve engine, an intake backfire can swell the rubber vacuum hose to the brake booster and knock it off, removing power assist.
issues.next: Brakes still work, but you must press much harder. Check your VIN for open recalls at a Lincoln or Ford dealer or nhtsa.gov; the repair is free.

issues.sym: The airbag warning light may come on. In rare cases the driver airbag can go off without a crash.
issues.why: A clockspring jumper wire can rub against the airbag horn plate and short out.
issues.next: Do not ignore an airbag light. Check your VIN for open recalls at a Lincoln or Ford dealer or nhtsa.gov; the repair is free.

issues.t: ABS warning light may not come on (recall)
issues.sym: If the anti-lock brake system fails, the warning light may stay off, so you would not know.
issues.why: A software error in the instrument cluster can stop the ABS warning light from turning on.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls at a Lincoln or Ford dealer or nhtsa.gov; the repair is free.

issues.sym: The wipers stop moving, often after long high-speed driving in rain.
issues.why: Some wiper motors were built without grease on a gear, which can then distort or break.
issues.next: Pull over safely if wipers fail in bad weather. Check your VIN for open recalls at a Lincoln or Ford dealer or nhtsa.gov; the repair is free.
